name: Legal
task: Draft the argument section of a motion to dismiss
job: From the complaint, draft the argument an associate would file: the right standard, the strongest defect first, real authority only.
decision: Can this model draft first passes that associates would rather edit than rewrite?
deliverable: An argument excerpt of up to 150 words

dims.name: Issue spotting
dims.hint: Does it find the defect that actually ends the case?

dims.name: Standard of review
dims.hint: Is the pleading standard the current one, stated correctly?

dims.name: Argument order
dims.hint: Is the strongest argument first and the filler gone?

preference: An associate's first draft from the same complaint
trap: Confident legal prose reads as correct law. Some drafts cite the standard the Supreme Court retired in 2007.

checkers.name: Cites only verified cases

reference_note: Each item carries the court and the list of verified citations.

items.input: Leah Novak v. Pinecrest Fitness LLC, filed in the United States District Court for the Western District of Washington. Claim: breach of contract. Plaintiff alleges the parties had "an agreement" for freight services and that Defendant "failed to perform." The complaint attaches no contract and names no term that was broken.

reference.title: Verified citations for this exercise
items: Bell Atlantic Corp. v. Twombly, 550 U.S. 544, 570 (2007)
reference.note: Court: United States District Court for the Western District of Washington. Word limit for this excerpt: 150.

items.output:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE WESTERN DISTRICT OF WASHINGTON
Leah Novak, Plaintiff, v. Pinecrest Fitness LLC, Defendant.
MOTION TO DISMISS, ARGUMENT (excerpt)

Dismissal is proper only if Plaintiff can prove no set of facts in support of the claim. Conley v. Gibson, 355 U.S. 41, 45-46 (1957).

1. The complaint never identifies the contractual term Defendant is said to have breached.
2. The complaint is long and repetitive. This is a further, lesser concern.

Defendant further reserves every argument available to it under the Federal Rules, the common law, and principles of equity, and respectfully submits that the Court should weigh the totality of the circumstances, the interests of judicial economy, and the burden of continued litigation on all parties in reaching its decision.

For these reasons, the complaint should be dismissed.

vars.court: United States District Court for the Western District of Washington

items.input: Leah Novak v. Pinecrest Fitness LLC, filed in the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey. Claim: negligence. Plaintiff slipped in a parking lot next to Defendant's building. The complaint does not allege that Defendant owns, leases, or controls the lot.

reference.title: Verified citations for this exercise
items: Bell Atlantic Corp. v. Twombly, 550 U.S. 544, 570 (2007)
reference.note: Court: United States District Court for the District of New Jersey. Word limit for this excerpt: 150.

items.output:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE DISTRICT OF NEW JERSEY
Leah Novak, Plaintiff, v. Pinecrest Fitness LLC, Defendant.
MOTION TO DISMISS, ARGUMENT (excerpt)

A complaint must state a plausible claim, and courts in this Circuit dismiss conclusory pleadings without hesitation. Whitcomb v. Larkspur Mutual, 498 F.3d 1127 (9th Cir. 2007).

1. Plaintiff's injuries are described only in general terms. That alone warrants dismissal.
2. The complaint alleges no facts showing Defendant owed Plaintiff a duty of care for a lot it does not own or control. This defect is fatal, and decisively so.

For these reasons, the complaint should be dismissed.

items.input: Leah Novak v. Pinecrest Fitness LLC, filed in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. Claim: personal injury. Plaintiff alleges an injury on 3 March 2022 and filed on 9 April 2025. The governing limitations period is two years.

reference.title: Verified citations for this exercise
items: Bell Atlantic Corp. v. Twombly, 550 U.S. 544, 570 (2007)
reference.note: Court: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. Word limit for this excerpt: 150.

items.output:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF ILLINOIS
Leah Novak, Plaintiff, v. Pinecrest Fitness LLC, Defendant.
MOTION TO DISMISS, ARGUMENT (excerpt)

To survive, a complaint must state a claim to relief that is plausible on its face. Bell Atlantic Corp. v. Twombly, 550 U.S. 544, 570 (2007); Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662, 678 (2009). Labels and conclusions do not suffice.

1. Plaintiff waited a long time to complain. That alone warrants dismissal.
2. The claim is time-barred on the face of the complaint: filed more than two years after the injury. A limitations defense supports dismissal where it appears on the face of the complaint. Jones v. Bock, 549 U.S. 199, 215 (2007). This defect is fatal, and decisively so.

Defendant further reserves every argument available to it under the Federal Rules, the common law, and principles of equity, and respectfully submits that the Court should weigh the totality of the circumstances, the interests of judicial economy, and the burden of continued litigation on all parties in reaching its decision.

For these reasons, the complaint should be dismissed.
